review_notes: I read the whole file from the supplied text and did not open any related sources. The only repetition is of two kinds. (1) The cofibrant and fibrant halves are formal duals of each other. Merging them would need a self-dual formulation, which the library does not provide here. (2) Within each half, the `coprod.inl`/`coprod.inr` instances and the `prod.fst`/`prod.snd` instances share a short proof. That proof is a rewrite with `isCofibrant_iff` (or `isFibrant_iff`) and `cofibration_iff` (or `fibration_iff`), followed by one call to `MorphismProperty.of_isPushout` (or `of_isPullback`) on an existing `IsPushout.of_isColimit_binaryCofan_of_isInitial` (or pullback) lemma, with `.flip` on one side. Each proof is about four lines, and the only difference is the `.flip`. A shared lemma would mostly move that branch into a helper, and the rubric says that is not enough. I found no nontrivial repeated reasoning that justifies a new lemma. I am slightly unsure only because I did not check whether the shared pushout shape could be factored more cleverly.
